## Load in data

We will load in an unfiltered pre-processed version of the raw data. See CzeLex_norms_preproccessing.Rmd.

```{r message=FALSE}
#rating data
czlex_norming_filtered <- read_rds("raw_filtered_data/czelex_raw_filtered_ratings_data.rds")

#demographic data
czlex_norming_filtered_demographics <- read_rds("raw_filtered_data/czelex_raw_filtered_demographic_data.rds")

#word list variables
czlex_word_list_variables <- read_csv("additional_data/czlex_word_list_variables.csv")

#lexical decision data
czlex_ldt <- read_rds("additional_data/czlex_ldt_summaries.rds")

```

### Reliability

We will assess reliability of the ratings along each of the dimensions. Namely, we will employ one-way intra-class correlation coefficients based on Brysbaert (2019)

ICC2

```{r}
for (i in unique(czlex_norming_filtered$dimension)) {
  
  mod1 <- lme(value1 ~ 1, random=~1|name, data = czlex_norming_filtered %>%
                filter(dimension == i),
              na.action=na.omit,
              control = lmeControl(opt = "optim"))
  
  cat(i, " ICC2 mean: ", mean(gmeanrel(mod1)$MeanRel), "\n")
  cat(i, " ICC2 weighted mean: ", weighted.mean(gmeanrel(mod1)$MeanRel, gmeanrel(mod1)$GrpSize), "\n\n")
  
  remove(mod1)

}

```

## Summary data

### Traditional descriptive statistics

First, we calculate the mean, SD, number of responses overall, number of responses where the word was known and the proportion of known responses, for each of the words across the dimensions.

```{r}
czlex_summary <- czlex_norming_filtered %>%
  group_by(name, dimension) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(value1, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd = sd(value1, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n(),
            n_known = sum(value_known),
            prop_known = n_known/n) %>%
  arrange(dimension, name)

czlex_summary %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 2))) %>%
  datatable(filter = 'top')

```

We will create a summary table in a wide format.

```{r}
czlex_summary_wide <- czlex_summary %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from  = dimension, values_from = c(mean, sd, n, n_known, prop_known))

czlex_summary_wide %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 2))) %>%
  datatable(filter = 'top')

```

Descriptive statistics: grand mean, standard deviation, minimum and maximum per dimension

```{r}
czlex_summary %>%

  summarise(Mean = mean(mean),

            Min = min(mean),
            Max = max(mean))

```

### Latent means using CLMM

Traditionally norms are summarised by the mean and SD. However, an alternative is presented by Taylor et al. (2021), who highlight that means are not always suitable for ordinal data, which our data is. We follow the advice of Taylor et al. and use cumulative link mixed models to extract the estimates for each word from models predicting the raw ratings, whilst also accounting for random variation from participant rating biases.

Taylor, J. E., Rousselet, G. A., Scheepers, C., & Sereno, S. C. (2021, August 3). Rating Norms Should be Calculated from Cumulative Link Mixed Effects Models. https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/3vgwk

We will convert the ratings to an ordered factor and then model the data using clmms for each dimension.

Note that for AoA we will not run this, a preliminary attempt at this led to major issues with the modelling. Although AoA values could be interpreted as ordinal, they appear not be suited for this type of modelling, even though there is a large amount of data.

We have also set the below chunks to not be evaluated in this document, as the can take some time to run. For efficiency, we extract the interception and stored them as a csv file, which can be quickly read in.

#### clmms

Concreteness

```{r eval=FALSE}
czlex_norming_filtered_concreteness <- czlex_norming_filtered %>%
  filter(dimension == "concreteness") %>%
  mutate(value1 = factor(value1, ordered = TRUE))

system.time(
  m_concreteness <- clmm(value1 ~ 1 + (1|name) + (1|subject),
                         data = czlex_norming_filtered_concreteness,
                         link = "probit")
  )

clmm_estimates_concreteness <- ranef(m_concreteness)$name %>%
  # store the item IDs in the item_id column rather than in row names
  as_tibble(rownames = "name") %>%
  # rename the random effects variable to something more informative than "(Intercept)"
  rename(clmm_concreteness = `(Intercept)`)

saveRDS(m_concreteness, file = "clmm_models/mods/concreteness_clmm.rds")
write_excel_csv(clmm_estimates_concreteness, file = "clmm_models/concreteness_clmm.csv")

```

#### brms

In the next sections, we will run a Bayesian model for each of the dimensions. These will operate in a very similar way to the clmm models above, i.e. they will be fitting the data in an ordinal way. However, we will also be adding in a model that provides with a latent SD estimate, this is the disc variable in the model, following Taylor et al's (2023) approach. As these models take a long time to run, we have set the below chunks to be not evaluated, to save time, each of them took approximately 14 hours to run and the resulting models are approximately 2.5GBIn size. We therefore extract all of the intercepts for the items and store them as CSV files for ease.

Concreteness

```{r eval=FALSE}
czlex_norming_filtered_concreteness <- czlex_norming_filtered %>%
  filter(dimension  == "concreteness") %>%
  mutate(rating = factor(value1, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(name1 = str_replace_all(name, " ", "."))

system.time(
  m_concreteness <- brm(
    brmsformula(
      rating ~ 1 + (1|name) + (1|subject),
      disc ~ 0 + (1|name) + (1|subject)
    ),
    data = czlex_norming_filtered_concreteness,
    family = cumulative("probit"),
    chains = 6,
    cores = 6,
    iter = 4000,
    control = list(
      adapt_delta = 0.95,
      max_treedepth = 10
    ),
    init = "0",
    file = file.path("brms_models/mods", "concreteness_m1.rds"),
    refresh = 100,
    seed = 3101,
    thin = 2
  )
)

item_estimates_concreteness <- map_df(unique(czlex_norming_filtered_concreteness$name1), function(i) {
  # on each iteration, create the strings to look up this item's random effects
  mu_re <- sprintf("r_name[%s,Intercept]", i)
  disc_re <- sprintf("r_name__disc[%s,Intercept]", i)
  # extract posterior samples for the random effects parameters, and calculate the median to get the estimate
  as_draws_df(m_concreteness, c(mu_re, disc_re)) %>%
    rename(mu = 1, disc = 2) %>%
    mutate(sd = 1/exp(disc)) %>%
    summarise(
      name = i,
      latent_mean_concreteness = median(mu),
      latent_disc_concreteness = median(disc),
      latent_sd_concreteness = median(sd)
    )
}) %>%
  rename(brms_concreteness = latent_mean_concreteness) %>%
  mutate(name = ifelse(!str_detect(name, "\\."), name,
                                   ifelse(str_detect(name, "\\.cz|\\.com"), name,
                                          ifelse(name == "SEV.en.energy", "SEV.en energy", str_replace_all(name, "\\.", " ")))))

rm(m_concreteness)

write_excel_csv(item_estimates_concreteness %>%
                  arrange(name),
                "brms_models/concreteness_brms.csv")

```

```{r message=FALSE}
brms_concreteness_estimates <- read_csv("brms_models/concreteness_brms.csv")
brms_gender_estimates <- read_csv("brms_models/gender_brms.csv")
brms_imageability_estimates <- read_csv("brms_models/imageability_brms.csv")
brms_valence_estimates <- read_csv("brms_models/valence_brms.csv")

czlex_summary_brms <- czlex_summary_wide %>%
  select(name) %>%
  left_join(brms_concreteness_estimates) %>%
  left_join(brms_gender_estimates) %>%
  left_join(brms_imageability_estimates) %>%
  left_join(brms_valence_estimates)

```

#### Merge all estimates together

```{r}
czlex_summary_clmm_brms <- czlex_summary_wide %>%
  left_join(czlex_summary_clmm) %>%
  left_join(czlex_summary_brms)

write_excel_csv(czlex_summary_clmm_brms, "czelex_summary_data.csv")

```

## Comparison of methods

In the below sections, we will be exploring whether the three different aggregation methods are related to each other. We will do this based on the item level estimates, looking at the mean, clmm and brms estimates. Similarly, we will also explore whether the variance estimates that have been derived from the SD and the latent SD from the brms models also have a clear relationship to the means and latent means, as well as to each other.

Item level estimates

```{r fig.height=6, fig.width=6, warning=FALSE}
czlex_summary_clmm_brms_comparison <- czlex_summary_clmm_brms %>%
  select(name, starts_with("mean_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(-name, names_to = "dimension", values_to = "mean") %>%
  mutate(dimension = str_remove(dimension, "mean_")) %>%
  left_join(czlex_summary_clmm_brms %>%
              select(name, starts_with("clmm_")) %>%
              pivot_longer(-name, names_to = "dimension", values_to = "clmm") %>%
              mutate(dimension = str_remove(dimension, "clmm_"))) %>%
  rename(x = mean,
         y = clmm) %>%
  mutate(comparison = "mean~clmm") %>%
  bind_rows(czlex_summary_clmm_brms %>%
              select(name, starts_with("mean_")) %>%
              pivot_longer(-name, names_to = "dimension", values_to = "mean") %>%
              mutate(dimension = str_remove(dimension, "mean_")) %>%
              left_join(czlex_summary_clmm_brms %>%
                          select(name, starts_with("brms_")) %>%
                          pivot_longer(-name, names_to = "dimension", values_to = "brms") %>%
                          mutate(dimension = str_remove(dimension, "brms_"))) %>%
              rename(x = mean,
                     y = brms) %>%
              mutate(comparison = "mean~brms")) %>%
  bind_rows(czlex_summary_clmm_brms %>%
              select(name, starts_with("clmm_")) %>%
              pivot_longer(-name, names_to = "dimension", values_to = "clmm") %>%
              mutate(dimension = str_remove(dimension, "clmm_")) %>%
              left_join(czlex_summary_clmm_brms %>%
                          select(name, starts_with("brms_")) %>%
                          pivot_longer(-name, names_to = "dimension", values_to = "brms") %>%
                          mutate(dimension = str_remove(dimension, "brms_"))) %>%
              rename(x = clmm,
                     y = brms) %>%
              mutate(comparison = "clmm~brms")) %>%
  mutate(comparison = factor(comparison, ordered = TRUE, levels = c("mean~clmm", "mean~brms", "clmm~brms"))) %>%
  filter(dimension != "aoa")

czlex_summary_clmm_brms_comparison_cor <- czlex_summary_clmm_brms_comparison %>%
  group_by(dimension, comparison) %>%
  summarise(cor = cor(x, y, use = "pairwise")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(cor1 = paste0("r = ", format(round(cor, 3), nsmall = 3)),
         cor1 = str_replace(cor1, "0.", "."))

```

## Correlations

```{r}
cor_data <- czlex_summary_clmm_brms %>%
  select(name, starts_with("mean_")) %>%
  left_join(czlex_word_list_variables %>%
              select(-frequency))

```

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.height=10, fig.width=10}
scatter_reg_curve <- function(data, mapping, ...) {
  ggplot(data = data, mapping = mapping) +
    geom_point(size = 0.05, alpha = 0.05) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "blue", se = FALSE, size = 0.7) + # Add regression curve
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", colour = "red", se = FALSE, size = 0.7, linetype = 2) + # Add regression curve
    theme_bw()
}

cor_func <- function(data, mapping, method, ...){
  x <- eval_data_col(data, mapping$x)
  y <- eval_data_col(data, mapping$y)
  
  corr <- cor(x, y, method=method, use='complete.obs')
  
  ggally_text(
    label = as.character(round(corr, 3)), 
    mapping = aes(),
    xP = 0.5, yP = 0.5,
    color = 'black',
    ...
  ) +
    theme_bw(base_line_size = 0)
}

# Creating the correlation matrix plot
plot_matrix <- ggpairs(
  cor_data %>%
    select(-name) %>%
    rename_with(~str_remove(.x, "mean_")),
  lower = list(
    continuous = wrap(scatter_reg_curve)
  ),
  diag = list(continuous = function(data, mapping, ...) {
                  ggally_densityDiag(data = data, mapping = mapping) +
                  theme_bw()}),
  upper = list(continuous = wrap(cor_func, method = "pearson", size = 4, stars = FALSE)),
  )

# Display the plot
plot_matrix

ggsave(plot_matrix, filename = "plots/correlation_plot_matrix.png", height = 10, width = 10, dpi = 400)

```

```{r}
coeffs_full <- summ(rt_model_mean, confint = TRUE, scale = TRUE)$coeftable %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("predictor") %>%
  mutate(model = "mean",
         predicted = "RT") %>%
  bind_rows(summ(rt_model_clmm, confint = TRUE, scale = TRUE)$coeftable %>%
              as.data.frame() %>%
              rownames_to_column("predictor") %>%
              mutate(model = "clmm",
                     predicted = "RT")) %>%
  bind_rows(summ(rt_model_brms, confint = TRUE, scale = TRUE)$coeftable %>%
              as.data.frame() %>%
              rownames_to_column("predictor") %>%
              mutate(model = "brms",
                     predicted = "RT")) %>%
  bind_rows(summ(acc_model_mean, confint = TRUE, scale = TRUE)$coeftable %>%
              as.data.frame() %>%
              rownames_to_column("predictor") %>%
              mutate(model = "mean",
                     predicted = "accuracy")) %>%
  bind_rows(summ(acc_model_clmm, confint = TRUE, scale = TRUE)$coeftable %>%
              as.data.frame() %>%
              rownames_to_column("predictor") %>%
              mutate(model = "clmm",
                     predicted = "accuracy")) %>%
  bind_rows(summ(acc_model_brms, confint = TRUE, scale = TRUE)$coeftable %>%
              as.data.frame() %>%
              rownames_to_column("predictor") %>%
              mutate(model = "brms",
                     predicted = "accuracy")) %>%
  rename(`Standardised coefficient` = 2,
         lower = `2.5%`,
         upper = `97.5%`) %>%
  mutate(predictor = ifelse(predictor == "zipf_frequency", "ZipfFreq",
                ifelse(predictor == "valence", "valence abs",
                       ifelse(predictor == "gender", "gender", predictor))),
         predictor = factor(predictor, ordered = TRUE, levels = c("valence abs", "imageability", "gender", "aoa", "old20", "ZipfFreq")),
         model = factor(model, ordered = TRUE, levels = c("mean", "clmm", "brms")),
         predicted = factor(predicted, ordered = TRUE, levels = c("RT", "accuracy")))

coeffs_full_plot <- coeffs_full %>%
  filter(predictor != "(Intercept)") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = `Standardised coefficient`, y = predictor, colour = model)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), size = 0.7, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.7, shape = 21, fill = "white", position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = .25) +

  facet_grid(~predicted, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        axis.title.y = element_blank())
```

```{r}
rt_concreteness_r2_tbl <- map_dfr(
  rt_concreteness_models,
  ~ summary(.x)$r.squared
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "predictor", values_to = "R2") %>%
  left_join(map_dfr(
    rt_concreteness_models,
```

```{r}
r2_tbl <- rt_r2_tbl %>%
  mutate(predicted = "RT") %>%
  separate(predictor, sep = "_", into = c("model", "predictor")) %>%
  bind_rows(acc_r2_tbl %>%
              mutate(predicted = "accuracy") %>%
              separate(predictor, sep = "_", into = c("model", "predictor"))) %>%
  mutate(r2_label = paste0(" adj R\u00B2 = ", format(round(`R2 adj`, 3), nsmall = 3), ", ΔR\u00B2 = ", format(round(delta_R2, 3), nsmall = 3))) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, ordered = TRUE, levels = c("mean", "clmm", "brms")),
         predicted = factor(predicted, ordered = TRUE, levels = c("RT", "accuracy")))

r2_full_plot <- r2_tbl %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = baseline_R2, y = predictor, colour = model)) +
  geom_linerange(data = r2_tbl,
                  aes(xmin = baseline_R2, xmax = `R2 adj`), size = 0.7, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.7, shape = 21, fill = "white", position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  geom_point(aes(x = `R2 adj`), size = 0.7, shape = 21, fill = "white", position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = baseline_R2), linetype = 2, linewidth = .25) +
  geom_label(aes(x = `R2 adj`, label = r2_label), position = position_dodgenudge(width = 0.8, x = 0.01), size = 2.5, hjust = 0, border.colour = "white", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_label(aes(x = baseline_R2-0.08, label = paste0("Baseline R\u00B2 = ", format(round(baseline_R2, 3), nsmall = 3)), colour = NULL), y = 2.5, text.colour = "black", size = 2.5, hjust = 0.5, angle = 270, border.colour = "white", show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.2, 1)), name = "Adjusted R\u00B2") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#004488", "#BB5566", "#DDAA33")) +
  facet_wrap(~predicted) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        axis.title.y = element_blank())

r2_full_plot

ggsave(plot = r2_full_plot, "plots/r2_full_plot.png", height = 4, width = 8, dpi = 400)
```
